milestones.name: Each module's record of what it copied, from where and under what licence is tracked in Git, where a clone gets it
milestones.quality_bar: As dependable as the third-party notices of a well-kept open-source project such as wgpu or Bevy: anyone with a clone can read what was copied, from where and under what licence, and the record is the one that gets updated.

items.statement: The provenance records of `SEA`, `WATERS`, `CLOUDS`, `PUDDLES` and `RIVERS` are tracked in Git as `docs/provenance/<MODULE>.md`. Each says what its working-folder record said about what was copied or translated, from where and under what licence. Every link in one resolves in a clone: a link to a file only the working folder holds becomes that file's name in plain text. The repository map says the folder holds these records.
items.check: sh -c 'test "$(git ls-files docs/provenance/SEA.md docs/provenance/WATERS.md docs/provenance/CLOUDS.md docs/provenance/PUDDLES.md docs/provenance/RIVERS.md | wc -l)" -eq 5 && ! git grep -qE "\]\([^)]*orchestrate/evidence" -- docs/provenance/SEA.md docs/provenance/WATERS.md docs/provenance/CLOUDS.md docs/provenance/PUDDLES.md docs/provenance/RIVERS.md && ./dev check-docs'
items.ask: Compare each tracked record with the working-folder record it came from: is any statement about what was copied, its source or its licence lost or changed? Does each working-folder record now open with a line that names the tracked record as the one to keep current?
items.evidence: .orchestrate/evidence/DEAD-TOOLS/M5/record-diffs.txt (tracked vs working records: only link forms differ); .orchestrate/evidence/DEAD-TOOLS/M5/check.log

milestones.name: The check refuses a new script or bench that nothing runs, a new source file that names `docs/evidence`, and a new shader text edit: each count is frozen where it stands
milestones.quality_bar: As dependable as a lint baseline in a well-kept repository such as Chromium's or rust-lang's tidy checks: what is already there is counted once, one more is refused with a message that says what to write instead, and a correct landing is never refused.

items.statement: Four rules of the shape check each hold a count that can only fall, entered at the count of the commit this milestone lands on: `evidence-path`, `script-caller`, `bench-runner` and `shader-text-edit`, as the design defines them. A landing that adds one more of any of them fails `./dev check`, and the message says what to write instead. A new script that a done-when item's check names is not refused, whether its milestone is open or Done, and no record under `docs/evidence` counts as naming a script or a bench. The log gives each rule's count at landing.
items.check: sh -c 'python3 scripts/shape_rules.py check --rule evidence-path && python3 scripts/shape_rules.py check --rule script-caller && python3 scripts/shape_rules.py check --rule bench-runner && python3 scripts/shape_rules.py check --rule shader-text-edit && python3 scripts/test_shape_rules.py'
items.ask: Read each rule's fixtures: does each refuse one more of its shape and pass the cases the design leaves out (the evidence store's restore code; a script that `dev`, a tracked document outside the plans or a done-when item's check names, for an open milestone and for a Done one; a suite named for no script; a bench a script runs; a `.replace(` in a test file)? Is a script or bench that only a file under `docs/evidence` names counted? In a scratch copy, add a script nothing names, and a `.replace(` to a non-test Rust file that mentions WGSL: does `./dev check` fail on each and say what to do? Count `shader-text-edit` by hand with `git grep`, and pick three scripts the rule counts and three it does not: do the log's counts and the rule agree with what you find?

items.statement: `./dev check` finds the script suites itself: every `scripts/test_*.py` runs, and every `scripts/test_*.mjs` where node is installed, with no list to keep, so a suite added later runs without an edit to the check. The record gives the time the newly run suites add to a check.
